items.summary: People familiar with the matter said Alphabet has recently discussed offering its first Hong Kong and Singapore dollar bonds, a deal that could test Asian investor appetite after an AI sell-off. The company reportedly sought to raise up to US$1 billion in Hong Kong dollars and around US$1.5 billion in Singapore dollars for general corporate purposes. Discussions remain ongoing with details subject to change.
items.title: Alphabet Weighs Hong Kong and Singapore Bond Sale Amid AI-Driven Volatility

items.summary: Korea's Ministry of Science and ICT and NVIDIA hosted the MSIT-NVIDIA AI Startup Partnership Forum at COEX, where vice minister Ryu Je-myung joined NVIDIA leaders to meet over 20 Korean startups across foundation models, physical AI, AI infrastructure and semiconductors. NVIDIA announced an investment in Point2, with additional planned investments in Motif Technologies, RLWRLD and Upstage. The commitments build on NVIDIA's work with Korea's startup community through its NVIDIA Inception program.
items.title: NVIDIA Announces Planned Investments in Korean AI Startups at Partnership Forum

items.summary: Hyundai Motor Group, AIM Intelligence, and LG AI Research are advancing secure agentic AI through partnerships with NVIDIA. Hyundai explores NemoClaw blueprints and OpenShell runtime; AIM integrates its Starfort platform to detect malicious instructions and data leakage while safeguarding enterprise tools; LG opens API access for K-EXAONE-2.5 built on Nemotron datasets, including the 7 million synthetic Korean personas in Nemotron-Personas-Korea.
items.title: Korea Partners With NVIDIA on Secure Agentic AI Models and Runtime

items.summary: On Wednesday, wildlife conservationist Jamie Robins of Buglife led a small protest outside Google's London headquarters, presenting a petition signed by almost 55,000 people against plans to build a large data center in Thurrock. The campaign is an alliance of special-interest groups worried about habitat loss for rare plants and bumblebees, pollution from the site—which Foxglove says could emit up to 570,000 tonnes annually—and the return of racing at the former Arena Essex motorcycle stadium. Google argues its plans prioritize biodiversity and emissions reduction, aiming for carbon neutrality by 2030. Protesters say they will continue resisting through lengthy planning campaigns. Thurrock Council expects to rule on the application early next year.
items.title: Wildlife and Biker Groups Protest Google's Thurrock Data Center

items.summary: A Goldman Sachs survey finds big investors are not abandoning private markets even as geopolitical tensions, high interest rates and slower exits make it harder to recoup capital. About 84% of institutional respondents plan to maintain or increase their exposure, matching the 83% in 2025. The study drew on 255 limited partners surveyed between June and August 2026. Jeff Fine of Goldman Sachs Alternatives called the AI infrastructure buildout a major deployment window, while Marc Nachmann noted investors are growing more selective. Singapore remains central to private equity activity in South-east Asia, with EY citing it for over 74% of regional deal value in 2025.
items.title: Goldman Survey Finds Investors Keep Betting on Private Markets Amid Slow Exits

items.summary: Chinese AI companies are increasingly hiring U.S.-based engineers, with MiniMax listing around 16 San Francisco openings and Seed advertising 71 positions. Experts say the move reflects a strategic shift toward talent access rather than homegrown recruitment, though success is limited by lower compensation—MiniMax paid roughly $203,000 per person versus OpenAI's up to $445,000 base salary—and weaker career prospects for frontier models. A Carnegie China study notes the U.S. gained 2,145 researchers while China lost 1,729 in 2025. Researchers warn hiring plans may not translate into hires as top talent favors American work culture and pay.
items.title: Chinese AI Firms Poach Silicon Valley Talent Amid Salary Gap

items.summary: Jaskon Engineers Limited plans to operationalise an initial 3 GW of integrated ingot, wafer and solar cell manufacturing in India by end-2028. Managing Director Ivan Saha told pv magazine the company may later expand capacity toward 10 GW for wafers and up to 5 GW for cells, depending on market conditions. The strategy emphasises vertical integration over external suppliers, with plans to adopt TOPCon 3.0 technology targeting cell conversion efficiencies of 25.5% to 25.6%. Saha also noted India has roughly 17 GW of ALMM-compatible TOPCon capacity at around 60% utilisation, implying possible annual production near 10 GW, though some output supports captive module manufacturing.
items.title: Jakson Aims for 3 GW Integrated Capacity by 2028

items.summary: Ahead of the COP31 climate summit in Antalya, Turkey, negotiators are expected to launch a “just transition mechanism”, widely known as the Belém-Antalya mechanism (BAM). The idea grew from years of civil-society advocacy and formal work under a 2015 Paris Agreement commitment. At COP30 in Brazil parties agreed to establish it after disagreements between developed and developing countries over its functions, financing and scope continued into Bonn talks in June 2026. Civil society groups such as the International Trade Union Confederation’s Bert De Wel, Climate Action Network’s Anabella Rosemberg and War on Want’s Leon Sealey-Huggins say a coordinated institutional home could centralise support for workers and communities shifting to low-carbon economies. However, details remain vague amid concerns about cost against UNFCCC funding gaps, with COP31 seen as the moment to move from talk into action.
items.title: Civil society pushes for just-transition mechanism at COP31

items.summary: After a gas furnace leak forced Sherry Frazier and her daughter out of their Baltimore home, the nonprofit Green & Healthy Homes Initiative (GHHI) coordinated an extensive retrofit. Workers replaced the roof, added insulation, installed safety features, and swapped every gas appliance for electric ones, then added rooftop solar in July 2025. The work totaled about $73,200 at no cost to Frazier. Her monthly bill fell from about $230 before electrification; savings came down further after going solar to around $170 per month as of May. GHHI found winter bills spiked to about $600–$700 when a snow cover blocked the heat pump, prompting her to leave it unencumbered year-round.
items.title: Retiree's Gas Leak Home Becomes All-Electric After Nonprofit Retrofit

items.summary: In Christiania, Tenn., Silicon Ranch operates a 3.25-megawatt solar project housing cattle under the panels. Terry Jennings of Electric Power Research Institute noted that designing facilities for grazing adds cost and uncertainty remains about how cows interact with panels. Loran Shallenberger said he did not expect it to work this well. The company held fortification costs at 3% over standard design, selling power below wholesale rates. Cattle reduce mowing needs significantly, performing better under the solar canopy than in open range.
items.title: Silicon Ranch Cattle Grazing Solar Fields in Tennessee

items.summary: German manufacturer Solarwatt launched the Panel vision M 5.0 construct, a bifacial tunnel oxide passivated contact (TOPCon) half-cut cell module aimed at building-integrated photovoltaic applications such as carports and facades. The company said it received general building authority approval from the German Institute for Construction Technology in January 2026, joining portfolio products certified since 2020.
items.title: Solarwatt launches bifacial TOPCon module for building-integrated solar use

items.summary: This article outlines five ways readers can prepare for the extreme weather that El Niño may bring this winter, including heavy rain, flooding, and snowfall. The steps cover signing up for local emergency alerts, identifying reliable information sources such as the National Weather Service and NOAA, packing an emergency kit with guidance from FEMA, protecting home and property against both flood and cold damage, planning evacuation routes, and following safety practices during power outages or contact with floodwaters. Several tips are drawn directly from agencies like FEMA, the Red Cross, and the North Carolina Department of Health and Human Services.
items.title: Five Steps to Prepare for El Niño Winter Weather

items.summary: An apparent honeytrap scandal involving Nvidia boss Jensen Huang and a suspected Chinese spy is shaking the AI sector, prompting an independent investigation. China denies spying claims as Nvidia shares fall amid market uncertainty over national security concerns.
items.title: Nvidia Honeytrap Scandal Rocks AI Sector Amid China Spy Claims

items.summary: US tech company Nvidia has opened an independent investigation after reports that its chief executive, Jensen Huang, had a relationship with businesswoman Alice Huang. The BBC describes her as a suspected Chinese spy. Reports question whether the scandal could damage his reputation despite his long tenure and public standing.
items.title: Nvidia Launches Probe Into Jensen Huang's Alleged Affair With Suspected Spy

items.summary: Tesla will refund many Cybertruck deposits because orders far exceed production capacity, CEO Elon Musk said on Monday. The wind-down follows last week's announcement that the electric vehicle maker is ending pickup truck production at its Texas factory in about 8 months. US sales fell 48 per cent to 20,237 units last year, according to Kelley Blue Book.
items.title: Tesla To Refund Many Cybertruck Deposits as Demand Exceeds Production, Musk Says

items.summary: The Reserve Bank of India clarified that no change is being made to cheque book rules, calling a viral social media message false and misleading. The claim suggested old cheques would only work for payments up to Rs 50,000 from January 1, 2027. RBI urged people to rely on official announcements.
items.title: RBI Denies Viral Cheque Book Change Rumour

items.summary: Reports say HSBC India is negotiating to become a second banking partner for Apple Pay after Axis Bank, potentially by the end of fiscal 2026-27. Other banks like Kotak Mahindra are also exploring partnerships. Transaction fee sharing remains unresolved, possibly delaying expansion.
items.title: HSBC Prepares to Join Apple Pay in India Amid Bank Race

items.summary: The European Union agency EU-Lisa has sued IBM, French IT group Atos and Italian defence contractor Leonardo over repeated delays in developing its new smart border system. The Financial Times reported the legal proceedings on Monday, citing internal communications. EU-Lisa said the action relates to development delays rather than the operation of the Entry/Exit System.
items.title: EU-Lisa Sues IBM, Atos and Leonardo Over Border System Delays

items.summary: UN Women flagged in its 2026 Gender Snapshot that no gender-equality indicator is on track for 2030, with equality 171 years away. India’s Taaron Ki Toli (‘Gang of Stars’) curriculum, developed by the NGO Breakthrough and evaluated through a randomised trial led by J-PAL-affiliated researchers Seema Jayachandran, Diva Dhar, and Tarun Jain in Haryana from 2014, shifted students’ gender attitudes. Following those results, J-PAL South Asia and Breakthrough partnered with Punjab and Odisha governments to embed the programme across state-run schools, reaching nearly four million students annually by grades 6–8 and 6–10. Adaptation reflects local context: land ownership in Punjab, disaster management in Odisha.
items.title: India Scales Gender-Equity Curriculum to Four Million Students

items.summary: A cluster randomized trial in Bihar tested a three-day Theatre of the Oppressed program across 417 police stations and roughly 2,500 officers. About seven months later, treated officers showed more favorable attitudes toward gender-based violence; standardized audits one year on found they were 15 percentage points less likely to blame victims, dismissed fewer complaints, and made more referrals, with administrative records showing a 41 percent drop in registration delays.
items.title: Expressive Arts Intervention Reduces Bias Among Indian Police Officers

items.summary: The authors introduce TaskNet, an occupational taxonomy grounded in workers’ accounts of their everyday work. A mixed-initiative system interviewed 132 workers across six occupations and produced 202 accepted task statements from 2726 reports. Every statement was validated by 318 incumbents through 7923 ratings. Relative to the O*NET 31.0 database, TaskNet covers 75% of published tasks while adding 79 with no counterpart and refining 58; it also covers more held-out worker reports (89% vs. 79%) and job-posting activities (72.5% vs. 70.2%). The authors note that TaskNet changes AI-exposure estimates in both directions, raising them for Software Developers and Lawyers.
items.title: Stanford researchers build AI-era task inventory from worker interviews

items.summary: NPR's Steve Inskeep spoke with economist Gabriel Zucman about taxes on millionaires and billionaires, focusing on how such taxation affects the economy. The discussion is set to be released as audio later today.
items.title: Economist Discusses Taxing Ultra-Wealthy and Economic Impact

items.summary: The UK government's electric vehicle targets are expected to be reduced this week, a move welcomed by carmakers but opposed by environmental groups. Under current rules, 80% of new cars sold must be electric by 2030. Downing Street insists no decision has been made, describing its approach as pragmatic and balanced. Sustainability groups warn the change could undermine climate leadership ahead of COP31 in Turkey.
items.title: UK Government Faces Expected Cut to EV Sales Targets

items.summary: UK households planning green energy upgrades risk a nationwide installer shortage unless the government abandons its planned 1 April reintroduction of VAT on heat pumps, solar panels and batteries. The change could add up to £1,530 to a smart home system amid record demand driven by doubled gas prices. Industry groups warn it would disrupt installers, while Liberal Democrats call it policy madness.
items.title: UK households rush for green energy installers amid VAT hike fears

items.summary: The artificial intelligence semiconductor company Nvidia has launched an independent investigation into its CEO, Jensen Huang, after he acknowledged a romantic relationship with businesswoman Alice Huang — also known as Huang Le — who is suspected of spying for the Chinese government. The New York Times broke the story last month about suspicions that Huang may have been targeted by a Chinese espionage operation through his relationship with Huang Le, then a senior executive at Megaspeed International, which had purchased $4. 8 billion worth of Nvidia chips over two years. U. S. officials reportedly concluded in 1985 — as reported by the Times and other outlets — that Alice Huang shared information with China while collaborating on data center construction in Asia. Huang will continue leading the company for now; he apologized to employees, saying an apology cannot undo what he did. The board said it has no reason to believe Nvidia's secrets or U. S.
items.title: Nvidia Launches Probe Into Jensen Huang Over Alleged Chinese Ties

items.summary: Jensen Huang, Nvidia's chief executive, admitted on Nov 8, 2026 that he had been unfaithful to his wife in a message to employees. The revelation followed reports linking him to Alice Huang, identified by US officials as suspected of working for Chinese intelligence and helping circumvent export controls via Singapore firm Megaspeed International, which committed to buying US$2 billion worth of Nvidia chips. Nvidia launched an independent investigation into whether its chief executive was targeted by a foreign operation. China dismissed the espionage claims as baseless; Singapore denied conducting investigations but said police probes into Megaspeed continue. Huang defended his dealings with Megaspeed as normal and remained committed to protecting NVIDIA, while Nvidia shares fell in out-of-hours trading.
items.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang Faces Espionage and Infidelity Allegations

items.summary: US President Donald Trump defended Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang after reports linking him to a woman suspected of spying for China. Trump said he had not discussed the matter with Huang but called him 'a fine person' and, when asked about regretting inaction on intelligence regarding an alleged affair between Huang and a business executive accused by US intelligence of gathering information for Beijing, added that Huang is 'an honorable guy.'
items.title: Trump Defends Nvidia's Jensen Huang Amid Spy Allegations

items.summary: Tech stocks rose on Monday, partly recovering losses from a midterms rout tied to AI regulation fears and tariffs. Asian indices led gains: the Nikkei 225 added more than 3%, SK hynix and Samsung around 3% in Korea's Kospi, TSMC nearly 6% and Taiwan's Taiex 5%. Nvidia opened an investigation into CEO Jensen Huang after reports of a relationship with a suspected Chinese spy; the board said there was no reason to believe secrets were compromised. Sally Auld at National Australia Bank noted investors would watch whether gains are sustainable rather than short-covering, citing unresolved AI regulation and capital expenditure concerns.
items.title: Asian markets rebound as Nvidia investigation looms

items.summary: President Donald Trump called Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang an “honorable guy” on Sunday, defending him amid reports of a relationship with Alice Huang, an alleged Chinese intelligence operative. The New York Times reported that Secretary of State Marco Rubio oversaw a classified memo warning officials about the connection before Trump's May visit to China. Intelligence identified Huang after surveillance linked his communications to Alice Huang, whom counterintelligence said China recruited. Huang had been excluded from the delegation but joined Air Force One during an Alaska refueling stop after media attention. Trump declined to restrict Nvidia or Huang, reportedly citing the chipmaker's importance to US competitiveness.
items.title: Trump Defends Jensen Huang Amid Chinese Spy Reports

items.summary: China's self-driving technology is being deployed and tested on the roads of Singapore, according to a page that also carries cookie-notice text unrelated to the story. The test vehicles are described as equipped with advanced sensors that perceive road conditions in real time, identifying pedestrians, vehicles and even chickens crossing the road so they can make timely judgments and safe evasions. Through China-Singapore cooperation, autonomous driving is being adapted to local traffic scenarios, moving from research toward real-world use.
items.title: Chinese autonomous driving tested on Singapore roads

items.summary: The article presents digital innovation, especially satellite technology and cross-border data cooperation, as a growing driver of growth across the Asia-Pacific region. It points to China's BeiDou Navigation Satellite System (BDS), which has reached more than 140 countries and holds a market share of 58% in Belt and Road partner countries. The piece cites an annual BDS industry report suggesting applications will increasingly combine navigation with 5G, the Internet of Things and AI. It notes practical results such as BeiDou-based flood early-warning systems covering 80% of Pakistan's flood-prone areas, wheat yields up by 15%, and a Shenzhen e-station that has supported over 1,900 companies expanding overseas through partnerships with 55 operators in 32 countries. China also launched the Action Initiative for Jointly Building Global Open Artificial Intelligence at the 2026 World Internet Conference Wuzhen Summit, calling on nations to share computing resources and datasets.
items.title: China Frames Digital Innovation as Asia-Pacific Connectivity Driver

items.summary: The 2026 Kailas Ultra Tour Mt. Siguniang finished on November 7, gathering 2,750 runners across five distances in southwest China. The course averaged above 3,600 meters and topped out beyond 4,600 meters. This was the first edition since Siguniang Mountain became a UNESCO Global Geopark.
items.title: Runners complete first Kailas Ultra Tour on Siguniang Mountain

items.summary: Paul Chan, Hong Kong's financial secretary, said on Sunday the region will keep promoting mega events and upgrading facilities to boost high-value tourism. He noted recent major events drew global business leaders and visitors that injected momentum into the economy. Hong Kong's economy expanded 5. 2% year on year in the third quarter, with first-nine-month growth of 5. 1%, the fastest pace for the period in five years. Visitor arrivals rose 11. 8% year on year in October; retail sales grew 6. 4% in September and restaurant receipts increased 3. 1% in the third quarter.
items.title: Hong Kong's financial secretary outlines tourism and event plans

items.summary: Israel's president tapped Gadi Eisenkot, Benjamin Netanyahu's chief political rival, to form a new government. The appointment follows an inconclusive election that left the country's leadership in limbo.
items.title: Israel's President Appoints Netanyahu Rival Eisenkot to Form Government

items.summary: Police say the 24-year-old attacker in Poland's weekend mass shooting at Kraków's Main Market Square, which killed six people and injured others, has died in hospital. Justice minister Waldemar Zurek said the terrorism probe continues to establish whether he acted alone.
items.title: Poland's justice minister says investigation into Kraków shooting will continue after suspect dies

items.summary: Russell Brand is to be sentenced today at Southwark Crown Court after being found guilty of one rape and three sexual assaults between 2004-2009. Justice Joel Bennathan warned last week he faces a significant prison term, following denial of bail on flight-risk grounds.
items.title: Russell Brand Faces Sentencing After Rape Convictions

items.summary: President Donald Trump said on Sunday that his proposal for UFC boss Dana White to become White House press secretary was 'just a little fun' and 'only kidding'. The role became vacant in October when Katie Zacharia left after less than five days. Trump posted the offer Saturday, saying he wanted fighters as assistants to defend against what he called the 'Lunatic Left.' White declined to confirm taking it ahead of their Monday meeting. He leads UFC, PowerSlap and Zuffa Boxing, and sits on Meta's board.
items.title: Trump says he was joking about Dana White press secretary offer

items.summary: British historian Sir Richard Evans, Regius Professor Emeritus of History at the University of Cambridge, argues that Adolf Hitler's Eagle's Nest in the Bavarian Alps was 'a Nazi vanity project.' He concludes it should be restored to its natural state. The controversy raises questions about preserving historical evidence versus removing symbols a criminal regime used to glorify itself.
items.title: Historian Calls Hitler's Eagle's Nest a Nazi Vanity Project for Destruction

items.summary: In Ghaziabad, on the outskirts of India's capital and among the world's worst air pollution, cigarette salesman Kanwar Singh, 55, works outside in toxic dust. He said: 'It enters my throat and lungs,' running his hands over clothes coated in fine particles. Only after drinking hot water and gargling can he breathe easily.
items.title: Cigarette Seller Describes Life Under Delhi's Dirtiest Air

items.summary:
Global environmental groups are adopting artificial intelligence for climate and wildlife work while warning it drives rising electricity, water and emissions from data centers. They cite a Reuters survey of 15 organizations and project the global footprint could double by 2030, prompting calls at COP31 to curb its growth.

items.summary: Western Australia's Minister for Aboriginal Affairs Don Punch visited South Hedland amid criticism of his handling of child protection failures, slamming the politicisation of the crisis and rejecting calls for his resignation. The town drew attention after reports of children in squalid conditions and a coronial inquest into 2022 deaths of three Aboriginal children in Port Hedland. Opposition figure Robert Isaacs launched a petition demanding Punch's removal, while Premier Roger Cook defended him as doing a great job.
items.title: WA Aboriginal Affairs Minister Defends Role Amid Child Protection Backlash

items.summary: Russia's second-largest oil refinery in the Leningrad region, Kirishi, was set on fire after a Ukrainian drone attack on Monday, according to Governor Alexander Drozdenko. The fire has been contained, but one woman died from falling drone debris and an apartment building was damaged. Russian air defence forces reportedly downed 113 drones during the overnight strikes.
items.title: Ukrainian Drone Attack Sets Russia's Kirishi Refinery Ablaze

items.summary: Poland's regional police said on Monday that the alleged perpetrator of Saturday's shooting rampage in Krakow died two days after being critically wounded by officers. The 24-year-old man, who allegedly killed his parents and sister before attacking a tourist area near the Old Town square, is suspected of killing six people and wounding 15. Poland has declared mourning as gun ownership rises across the country.
items.title: Krakow Mass-Shooting Suspect Dies in Hospital

items.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin addressed the 14th meeting of security council secretaries from Commonwealth of Independent States member states in Moscow on November 9, 2026. He emphasized using their analytical and forecasting capabilities amid global conflict escalation, stressing objective assessment of developments to protect citizens and ensure organizational stability.
items.title: Putin Urges CIS Security Councils to Leverage Capabilities for Stability

items.summary: Radin Besharati Loroun, representative of the Iran-China Chamber of Commerce and Industries in China, described the CIIE as a valuable platform. He said it lets Iranian businesses showcase their products, promote Iranian culture, and tap into the Chinese market.
items.title: Iranian Businesses Use CIIE as Platform for Chinese Market Access

items.summary: At the China International Import Expo, Takeshi Yoshida, president of Sony (China) Co., Ltd., told CGTN that the event is more than a showcase for technology. He described it as an ideal place for companies to find partners and pursue co-creation in China.
items.title: Sony Calls CIIE Key Platform for China Partnerships and Co-creation

items.summary: Nvidia shares fell overnight as CEO Jensen Huang acknowledged an affair with Alice Huang and apologised to staff in a message released Sunday. Analysts see the November 17 earnings report as the key test, noting sentiment may dip but long-term impact depends on whether leadership changes occur. Chris Weston warned that if she is confirmed as a spy, shares could fall sharply. Bill Ackman hoped for a simple affair rather than a national security risk. Trump called Huang a fine person without discussing it directly.
items.title: Analysts Warn Nvidia Stock Could Fall Sharply After Huang Affair

items.summary: Reuters reports that Nvidia's board is investigating whether CEO Jensen Huang was targeted by a foreign intelligence effort, following a New York Times report linking him to Alice Huang, whom US authorities concluded was a Chinese intelligence asset. Reuters could not independently verify the claims or confirm her current employment with Megaspeed.
items.title: Nvidia Board Launches Probe into Jensen Huang Over Alleged Foreign Intelligence Ties

items.summary: Nvidia Corp. said on Sunday it was opening an investigation into CEO Jensen Huang after he acknowledged a romantic relationship with a business executive whom US intelligence determined was a Chinese spy. With only a 3. 4% stake, Huang remains the architect of Nvidia’s strategies; his direct reports number as many as 60 according to Bernstein Research. The revelation is shaking up the AI world as national security risks surface and Asian banks grow more comfortable with chip financing. Its corporate bond spread has widened, and its $4.
items.title: Jensen Huang is bigger than Nvidia. It’s a problem

items.summary: Nvidia shares fell more than 4% in after-hours trading on Monday, dropping from $186.64 to around $178.60 as an internal investigation examined whether chief executive Jensen Huang had been targeted by a foreign intelligence operation following media reports of his relationship with Alice Huang, whom US authorities said was a Chinese intelligence asset. The inquiry has drawn scrutiny over Huang's future at the AI chipmaker and raised national security concerns from senior Republicans in the US House. Nvidia maintained its board has 'no reason to believe' that company secrets were compromised while an independent committee reviews available information.
items.title: Nvidia Shares Fall After Jensen Huang Admits Affair and Faces Investigation

items.summary: China rejected allegations that it ran an espionage operation targeting Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, calling the claims baseless and a smear. Foreign ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun said the narrative of a Chinese spy is entirely baseless vilification and smearing. The denial follows reports that Nvidia's board launched an independent investigation into whether Alice Huang was recruited by China to gather information about Huang.
items.title: China Denies Espionage Allegations Against Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang

items.summary: Beijing denied on Monday a report of a spy plot targeting Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, calling the allegations unsubstantiated and a smear campaign against China. Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun stated the claims were baseless. The controversy centers on whether Huang drove sales of advanced chips to China despite US restrictions, prompting an internal investigation.
items.title: China Rejects Spy Allegations Against Nvidia's Jensen Huang as Smear Campaign

items.summary: Alice Huang, also known as Huang Le, faces allegations that she was recruited by China's Ministry of State Security to gather information about Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and influence the chipmaker. Reports from The New York Times and Financial Times cite a classified memo suggesting she aimed to affect sales of advanced AI chips to China while export restrictions were in place. Nvidia has opened an investigation into possible foreign intelligence activity targeting its chief executive, who acknowledged infidelity without naming her. Claims remain under scrutiny, with the Chinese government rejecting them as groundless.
items.title: Chinese Woman Alleged Nvidia Spy Under Scrutiny Amid Intelligence Claims

items.summary: DeepSeek disclosed that its open-source agent application, DeepSeek Harness, reached approximately 1.54 million daily active users by November 4, less than three months after its August 13 debut. The figure is based on the number of users connecting to its own servers and was shared Sunday on X.
items.title: DeepSeek Reports AI Agent Platform Reaches 1.54 Million Daily Users

items.summary: Google parent Alphabet is reportedly considering raising up to $3 billion through bond offerings denominated in Hong Kong and Singapore dollars, per a Bloomberg report. Discussions are preliminary as early as November, with proceeds for general corporate purposes. The move comes amid growing investor concern over technology companies' heavy spending on AI infrastructure.
items.title: Alphabet Weighs Up To $3 Billion Asia Bond Sale Amid AI Spending Fears

items.summary: The article profiles nine technology executives whose conduct drew scrutiny, opening with Nvidia's Jensen Huang. Huang told employees via email that he was unfaithful while the board opened an independent investigation into reports of a foreign intelligence effort; it said there is no reason to believe national security or company secrets were compromised and that he remains CEO during the probe. The list then covers Bill Gates over affairs linked by Epstein, Andy Byron's resignation after a kiss-cam photo, Josef Matosevic and Wolfgang Dangel for consensual relationships with employees, Ken Peterman whose firing was followed by an insider-trading arrest, Elon Musk over a 2018 harassment settlement of $250,000, Michael Goguen amid abuse allegations and a suit seeking more than $800 million, Brian Krzanich for violating Intel's non-fraternization policy, and Mark Hurd for breaking conduct rules while not breaching the sexual-harassment policy. Many figures disputed or denied the claims.
items.title: Nine Tech Executives Caught in Scandals Ranging from Infidelity to Espionage Allegations

items.summary: Nvidia's board launched an independent investigation after CEO Jensen Huang admitted in a November 2026 email that he had an affair with Alice Huang, whom US authorities suspect is a Chinese intelligence asset. The probe examines whether foreign intelligence targeted him and any risks to company secrets. Nvidia states there is no evidence of compromised national security or proprietary information.
items.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang Admits Affair, Faces National Security Probe

items.summary: A thick smog blanketed Delhi on Monday, with AQI readings above 400 at several stations a day after Diwali. BJP leaders blamed the previous Congress and AAP governments for failing to address the crisis; Kapil Mishra alleged Punjab stubble-burning was premeditated pollution sabotage. Pawan Khera questioned missing early-morning Delhi data, while Praveen Khandelwal accused AAP of allowing burning. Saurabh Bhardwaj charged BJP with manipulating figures.
items.title: Delhi Smog Row as Parties Clash Over Air Quality Data

items.summary: Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N Chandrababu Naidu said the alliance's popularity has grown since the 2024 elections, citing progress over two and a half years. Addressing a press conference in Amaravati on municipal polls, he stated the NDA alliance secured 58.9% of votes with a strike rate of 94%. He added that the YSR Congress Party lost over 6.25% of votes overall. Naidu called for discipline within the alliance and urged withdrawing ₹500 notes to promote digital currency in fighting corruption.
items.title: CM Naidu Credits Development for Rising NDA Popularity in Andhra Pradesh

items.summary: Haitian officials said they killed a major gang leader in the capital during a joint operation with other forces. The National Police attacked a stronghold in Cité Soleil and fatally wounded Mathias Saintil of the Boston gang. Interim Prime Minister Alix Didier Fils-Aimé posted on X that one less gang leader remained, while President Nayib Bukele said gangs would not be getting any sleep.
items.title: Haiti Kills Gang Chief as El Salvador, Mercenaries Add Pressure

items.summary: Senior Delhi journalist Ajaz Ashraf argues that Hindus in the United States and India should publicly reject Hindutva following Donald Trump's midterm defeat. His argument rests on a 2022 Los Angeles Times confessional by Akhila L. Ananth, who described her struggle between tradition and progressive values. Ashraf contends that Hindu politicians cannot counter Modi's polarising politics without an inclusive economic programme—citing Abdul El-Sayed and Nithya Raman as examples—and urges introspection after attacks on Hindu temples and symbols.
items.title: Hindu activists urged to oppose Hindutva after US election reversal

items.summary: Gadi Eisenkot, rival of incumbent Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, was given the first mandate to form Israel's next government after President Isaac Herzog formally tasked him following a hung assembly in the Oct. 27 election. The Associated Press reported neither bloc secured a clear majority. Among possible allies are Arab-led parties such as Ra’am and Joint List, though cooperation is politically fraught for both sides. Eisenkot set four conditions, including recognizing Israel as a Jewish state and declaring Hamas a terrorist group. He has up to six weeks, with 28 days initially plus a possible two-week extension; failing that, Netanyahu may attempt a coalition before early elections next spring. Trump called the two leaders similar in policy views.
items.title: Eisenkot Given First Chance To Form Israeli Government

items.summary: A Bengal BJP MLA, Papiya Adhikari, said bursting firecrackers helps cure many diseases while inaugurating a Kali Puja programme. The remark drew sarcastic online reactions as Kolkata faces air-quality concerns; its AQI reached 301, 'very poor', per CPCB data. Users mocked the claim, suggesting rebranding firecrackers as medicine or prescribing an AQI of 500 as immunity boosters.
items.title: Bengal BJP MLA's firecracker health claim goes viral amid Kolkata pollution

items.summary: Nuvama Wealth Management reported a net profit of Rs 304 crore for the quarter ended September, up from Rs 254 crore a year earlier. Revenue from operations rose 20.35 per cent to Rs 1,366 crore in July-September FY27 from Rs 1,135 crore a year ago, per the company's regulatory filing. Operating profits grew 26 per cent and return on equity held at 29 per cent. Client assets reached Rs 5.5 lakh crore, up 25 per cent. MD & CEO Ashish Kehair described it as another quarter of strong performance across wealth management, asset services and capital markets segments.
items.title: Nuvama Wealth Management Posts 19% Profit Rise in Q2 FY27 Results

items.summary: Police in Tamil Nadu reported ten unconnected murders from Sunday into Monday morning during the Deepavali celebrations. The victims included a Special Sub-Inspector of police in Theni and an auto-rickshaw driver hacked to death in Vyasarpadi, Chennai. Authorities formed special teams to trace absconding suspects. Police said most killings stemmed from intoxication, rowdy behaviour or sudden rage over firecrackers, while history-sheeter cases exploited festive distractions at night. The Greater Chennai Police deployed 18,000 personnel for Deepavali security.
items.title: Tamil Nadu Records Ten Murders on Deepavali Day, Including a Police Officer

items.summary: Congress Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi is expected to visit Manipur on November 26, meeting families displaced by ethnic violence between the Meitei and Kuki-Zo communities. The clashes began May 3, 2023; at least 306 people have been killed and 49 remain missing as of August 31, 2026, per state Assembly figures. Government data released in April showed more than 58,000 displaced, nearly 7,900 houses destroyed and over 2,600 partially damaged. Gandhi is also expected to meet Congress leaders ahead of early next year's Assembly elections.
items.title: Rahul Gandhi Planned Visit To Manipur Displaced Families

items.summary: Ashutosh Bhardwaj reviews Shantanu Nandan Sharma's debut book, Rebel Bastar: History, Maoism and the Search for Answers in India's Heartland (Hachette India; 320 pages; Rs.799). The work opens with a bold premise to trace contemporary naxalism in Bastar back through centuries of resistance rather than reduce it to Maoist arrival or foreign import. Bhardwaj, an independent writer and journalist, notes the promise begins to diminish as the book progresses into territory ill-suited for its enquiry. He criticises Sharma's simplistic distinction between Maoists and Adivasis, his reliance on surrendered cadres' retrospective testimony, and a breadth that sacrifices depth.
items.title: Review Finds Rebel Bastar Overpromises on History of Naxalism
